A: Headline counts are padded with hardcoded constants ('Open alerts' = queue+61, 'HIGH OPEN' = queue+16, lines 717-719): the band claims 81 open / 23 high while the queue holds 22, so clicking a fleet cell labelled 'EXM 11' returns only ~3 rows - visible count/filter inconsistency, even though a code comment declares the queue 'a sample'
Alert volume chart occupies the prime slot above the triage queue, pushing the queue's first row roughly a third down the page at 1600x1000
Large empty region under the 22-row queue on tall viewports (small sample dataset does not fill the primary panel)
B: Medium severity pill renders as 'MEDI' (sev.slice(0,4)) - sloppy truncation repeated on every medium row

Accessibility is thin: one aria attribute in the whole file, KPI filters are clickable divs (not buttons), queue rows are click-only and not keyboard focusable, no visible focus styling or prefers-reduced-motion handling
KPI deltas ('3 last hour' etc.) are hardcoded strings, not computed from the data they sit beside
Client load panel is clipped at the 1600x1000 fold (below-fold content, minor)

notes: Both are genuinely strong, functional SOC consoles: smoke tests confirmed working severity filters, search, cross-filters and state-mutating actions in each, with zero external dependencies. B wins on queue primacy (70% width, 87 reconciling rows) and internal data consistency, and its SLA-per-row and client-load cross-filter are sharp. A wins on the brief's 40-tenant dimension (all 40 visible as a filtering heat grid with hatched NO-DATA cells, 'unknown is not clean'), and decisively on usability/accessibility: keyboard-navigable rows, real buttons, aria labelling, focus rings and reduced-motion, where B is mouse-only. A's padded headline counts are its one real correctness blemish; B's mouse-only operation is the larger failure for a tool an analyst lives in all shift.
